summary: Dependency `libsignal` resolved from a mutable GitHub branch of the author's own repo
details: package.json declares the dependency `libsignal` with the source `github:dzytzy/alya-baileys#latest` instead of a registry version range. On `npm install`, npm fetches whatever that branch currently contains — no commit SHA, no integrity hash, no version pin — and executes any lifecycle scripts inside it. The author can change the bytes delivered under the name `libsignal` at any time, so every future install resolves and executes code from a mutable, author-controlled source. The dependency name shadows the well-known upstream crypto library `libsignal`, obscuring that resolution is redirected to a branch of the author's own repository. Separately, when a caller authenticates their WhatsApp session via `makeWASocket()`, the ChannelManager unconditionally adds the hardcoded newsletter `120363411407993897@newsletter` and auto-follows it with retries on connection open, performing reach-padding under the installer's identity.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
